subject: biology
promptStrong: Give me a 6-mark exam-style question on {lo} for {board} {level} {subject}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a worked example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: Which blood vessel carries blood from the heart to the lungs?
questions.explain: The pulmonary artery carries deoxygenated blood from the heart to the lungs.

questions.q: Active transport differs from diffusion because it:
options: Moves substances down the concentration gradient
Requires energy from respiration to move substances against the gradient
Does not require a cell membrane
questions.explain: Active transport moves substances against the concentration gradient and needs energy (ATP) from respiration.

questions.q: Why do capillaries have walls that are one cell thick?
options: To allow efficient exchange of substances by short diffusion distance
questions.explain: Thin capillary walls give a short diffusion path for exchange of oxygen, nutrients and waste.

questions.q: Why do single-celled organisms NOT need a transport system?
options: They use active transport for everything
They have a large surface area to volume ratio so diffusion is sufficient
questions.explain: Their large surface area to volume ratio and short diffusion distances allow exchange by diffusion alone.

questions.q: Which gas diffuses from the alveoli into the blood?
questions.explain: Oxygen diffuses from the high concentration in the alveoli into the blood.

questions.q: Why does the left ventricle have a thicker muscular wall than the right ventricle?
options: It pumps blood only to the lungs
It pumps blood at high pressure all around the body
questions.explain: The left ventricle must generate enough pressure to pump blood around the whole body.

questions.q: A piece of potato is placed in pure (distilled) water. What is most likely to happen to its cells?
options: Water leaves the cells and they become flaccid
Sugar diffuses out of the cells
Water enters the cells by osmosis and they become turgid
questions.explain: Pure water is more dilute than the cell contents, so water enters by osmosis, making cells turgid and increasing mass.

questions.q: As an organism gets larger, its surface area to volume ratio:
questions.explain: Larger organisms have a smaller surface area to volume ratio, so they need specialised exchange surfaces and transport systems.

questions.q: What is the function of valves in the heart and veins?
questions.explain: Valves ensure blood flows in one direction only and prevent backflow.

questions.q: In a leaf, which structures allow gases to enter and leave?
questions.explain: Stomata are small pores, mainly on the lower leaf surface, that allow gas exchange.

questions.q: Which part of the blood mainly transports dissolved substances such as carbon dioxide, urea and nutrients?
questions.explain: Plasma is the liquid that transports dissolved substances around the body.

questions.q: What is the main role of platelets?
questions.explain: Platelets are cell fragments that help the blood clot at wounds.
